long_biography.plain_text:
The acquisition of IBP reshaped Tyson Foods during John H. Tyson's tenure as chief executive. It added major beef and pork operations to a business long identified with chicken, and made the company a much broader food processor. Tyson had prepared for that responsibility by working in almost every department from his teenage years.

Tyson now governs the business as board chairman, drawing on experience that stretches from operations and sales to senior management. His individual shareholding and interests through Tyson Limited Partnership give him a substantial financial stake. The partnership's high-vote shares retain family control, while the chief executive role belongs to a separate operating leader.
